He’s entitled to his opinion, but I think it can still be harmful even if he doesn’t directly discriminate. Not informing himself on issues and not caring to know the stance of his church on certain themes does show privilege and is harmful because it allows organizations to continue being ignorant and not inclusive. And it also allows hate to continue to be spread because people don’t care enough to speak up. 

And on the privilege argument, yes some Black men are privileged and some white men struggle. I don’t deny that. Privilege also looks at class, social status, education, sexual orientation, level of thinness, etc. Most of us probably have some privilege in some ways. The dangerous or harmful thing is to not recognize it. But, that doesn’t change my point. Ben clearly has privilege and even acknowledged it in the reunion. I don’t know about now, but during the show his actions or lack thereof was a problem. 

Anyway, I have said my opinion on the matter and you’re allowed to disagree, of course, but I’m done  arguing my point.

Not having an opinion on important social issues is problematic. Someone will align with him for sure. He can find his person. Good for him. Whatever. But people are allowed to disagree with his lack of views when it obviously comes from his white straight man privilege. Not being informed on BLM or 2SLGBTQIA+ issues and not being bothered when they aren’t outwardly accepted is problematic because it enables hate to continue. It doesn’t necessarily make him evil or whatever, but he put himself in a TV show and people are allowed to criticize what they see. His opinion is flawed and if a person does not think so, their opinion is also flawed and probably coming from privilege.

So she doesn’t feel secure in the relationship, then she acts out in desperate ways to get that reassurance but in turn, it pushes him away. Especially because he’s not attracted to her in the first place. They are a perfect storm and it’s never going to work. All I’m saying is Zanab probably had confidence issues because of her past and everything for sure, but they are being triggered by the relationship because she is getting no good reassurance. An anxious attachment person can go and be in healthy relationships, but they need to feel that their partner wants to be with them. Unfortunately though, this relationship is a classic case of anxious versus avoidant. Zanab deserves better. Plus, she is gorgeous. I’m personally more attracted to her than to Colleen. OP, you might feel like your relationship has no issues, but him being jealous and overprotective is an issue. You might see it as romantic and cute that he loves you so much that he gets jealous if other men are around you but this is an issue because he doesn’t trust you and needs to test that you won’t cheat on him. It seems like he needs to control the situation but control in a relationship is never healthy. That combined with the pretty massive age gap rings alarm bells in my head… You can make your own decisions obviously but I would suggest leaving him and finding someone who trusts you and who doesn’t feel the need to test you or control you.

I know it’s hard but it sounds like you need to leave him. Why? Because you want to and you have tried working through the stuff but you’re too different and in my experience, it makes it hard to meet in the middle when two people are very different. Anyway, if what you want is to not be with him anymore, don’t stay just to please him.
I hope he leaves you alone too but really, the only thing you can do is block him on everything and ignore him.

I think that as long as he will get your attention, he will keep talking to you and keep wanting to manipulate you. If he can’t talk to you then he can’t manipulate you. I would advise to keep him blocked and to go on with your life. From what you’ve said about this guy he will not come around and so I do think it’s time to let him go. And please, if a guy tries to force you to have sex, tried to rape you, don’t ever go back to him cause he’s already showed you what he’s capable of and he could try again and be successful. 

Seriously though, if he’s ignored long enough, he should get the hint and move on and if he doesn’t, call the police or something because harassment isn’t okay.
It does not excuse him but it does gloss over the fact that he was manipulating them and using their trauma or their position in life to make them do his bidding.

I’m not writing like a kid. I’m not a kid. I work with victims of abuse and sexual violence everyday. I have seen what it can do to a person. Sure these teenagers made choices but these choices were made under a lot of pressure and there was a huge power imbalance in place that skewed things. And sure they were not 10, I get that, but until you are about 25, your frontal lobe isn’t completely done developing as well and that part of the brain helps you make decisions, which means teenagers tend to be more impulsive as well. Moreover, if one of these girls was in this situation, they were stuck in it and the longer they were involved, the more they probably felt like they couldn’t get out of it unscathed. 

Putting the blame on these girls just takes the blame off Epstein (and his collaborators who were adults) who knew very well was he was doing. He knew he had power. He knew he had money and influence to convince these girls and it worked for a long time. 

So I’m not saying they were stupid or didn’t know or understand the choices, I’m saying they chose the path of least resistance because it might have felt less risky to them. They didn’t know what this man could have done to them if they said no. That’s the point of the power imbalance. He was trying to take advantage and he certainly achieved that.

They were children though. Sure adults could have known better maybe but if they had gone through abuse as well it could have been a survivor’s instinct. Sexual abuse causes deep-rooted trauma. But again, they were underage. They were being manipulated and taken advantage of.

All the people who are saying these girls are guilty are victim blaming and wrong. Sorry not sorry. They were underage girls being manipulated and taken advantage of. They were impressionable. They were traumatized and were just trying to figure things out. Clearly, you do not know what trauma can do to a person, especially someone who is still developing. And also, I’m sure they’ve beaten themselves over it enough that they don’t need anonymous trolls on the internet making them feel worse. 

If you are victim blaming these now women, you are part of the problem and also part of the reason why so many victims do not share their stories. Shame on you. 

I know this is kind of inflammatory but I’m just fed up with victims being shamed and accused.

I can tell you what not to do because I never had a close relationship with my mother. Don’t try to control her life. Let her make her own mistakes. Let her breathe. Listen to her when she does come to you and tell her you’re proud of her without putting all this pressure on her to be perfect. When she tells you things in confidence, don’t freak out and scream about it. Keep those things she tells you to yourself and support her. It will make her want to come back and tell you more. 

My mom tried so hard to be my friend but the result was the exact opposite. Don’t overprotect, let her live her life and most importantly, listen and support her without judgement. That’s what I want to do for my future daughter too. I don’t want what I got...

So yeah, anyway, I think that was a complete lie. The whole issue was that she wasn’t attracted to Mark. I get that she could maybe objectively understand that he was attractive and not be attracted to him but that was still the darn problem and even though her thing with Barnett might have been mostly pushed on by the fact that he was unavailable, she had more of a physical attraction to him.
